proseChanges.summary: **Legacy media and widget fidelity:** a legacy import now rewrites legacy storage URLs in imported message text, article bodies, the workspace logo, the widget background and teammate and assistant avatars to native URLs that serve the same bytes under native access rules: a conversation's file through its conversation, a logo, avatar or background to anyone (so the widget shows it on the customer's site), an article image to whoever may read an article that holds it. A URL whose file the package does not carry is left as written and counted (`mediaUrls` in the summary). The imported widget keeps legacy's look and behaviour: legacy's default colours under the saved overrides (the dashboard colour no longer recolours the launcher or send button), the schedule's days as numbers the dashboard reads and saves, no presence-based away, and the workspace shown as the team to an unassigned visitor; legacy keys the native widget does not read are listed (`widgetNotReproduced`). Apply `321_legacy_import_files.sql` after 320, then run `node scripts/legacy-import/upgrade.mjs --project <id>` once per workspace imported before this change. Documented in docs/LEGACY-EXPORT.md. **Fixes — Cloudflare Email Sending account binding:** the deploy declaration (`deploy.json`, and `management/integration/managed-deploy.json` generated from it) now binds `EMAIL_ACCOUNT_ID`, the name the Worker reads, as an optional secret beside `MAIL_ACCOUNT_ID`, so a normal deploy can enable Cloudflare Email Sending. Before, a deploy sent only `MAIL_ACCOUNT_ID` and never delivered `EMAIL_ACCOUNT_ID` to the Worker: an installation of v0.4.12 to v0.4.17 that set `EMAIL_PROVIDER=cloudflare` got outbound mail unavailable, so sign-in links could not be sent. The binding is optional, so installations on Resend or SendGrid, or without mail, are unaffected. `scripts/delivery/secret-declarations.mjs`, run by `verify:build`, now also fails when an `EMAIL_*` name the Worker reads is not bound in the declaration. Existing installations keep their bindings; set `EMAIL_ACCOUNT_ID` privately and redeploy to enable Cloudflare mail. No migration. **Fixes — setup and email-link sign-in during a knowledge upgrade:** an upgraded installation with imported history no longer answers `503` on `/api/identity/setup`, `/api/identity/setup-status`, `/api/identity/auth-options`, `/api/identity/sign-in-options`, `POST /api/identity/magic-link` and `POST /api/identity/magic-link/consume` while a workspace's knowledge conversion is unfinished (days on an installation with millions of imported rows). Those routes read no knowledge data, so password-less imported owners can request and use an emailed sign-in link at once, as password login and an existing session already could. The fence is otherwise unchanged: public knowledge pages and every other anonymous `/api/*` route (the customer widget, the portal, the public articles API) still answer `503` until every workspace's conversion finishes, and so do `forgot-password`, `link-status`, `accept-token`, `register` and `verify-email`. Member sessions are unaffected. No migration. **Migrations:** `321_legacy_import_files.sql`. Apply once after `320_legacy_import_work_repair.sql` and before serving the updated Worker; it is additive and creates one empty table.

proseChanges.ownerAction: Update from v0.4.17 without resetting. Back up D1, R2, Durable Object state and private settings first. Use Node 22.20.0, pnpm 10.12.4 and pinned rer 0.2.105. Retain native owners, permissions, support history, files, erasure fences and every applied migration identity. Apply the missing migrations once, in filename order, BEFORE the new Worker serves traffic: 321_legacy_import_files.sql. Earlier installations, including v0.4.16, also apply every intervening missing published migration in order (v0.4.16 also needs 320_legacy_import_work_repair.sql); retain each migration's buyer steps. After migration 321, run `node scripts/legacy-import/upgrade.mjs --project <legacy project id>` once per workspace imported from legacy, as the migration's buyer steps in RELEASE.json describe. To enable Cloudflare Email Sending, set `EMAIL_ACCOUNT_ID` privately and redeploy. Run `rer deploy --dry-run` against the retained installation before any separately authorized deployment. No reset, cutover or production deployment is part of this release. Live-provider qualification and owner cutover remain separate. Back up D1 first; apply once after 320_legacy_import_work_repair.sql, before serving the updated Worker. Additive only: creates the empty legacy_import_files table (imported legacy files that have no conversation: logos, the widget background, avatars and article images, served by /api/imported-files/<workspace>/<file>); no existing row changes and nothing is read, sent or queued. Then run node scripts/legacy-import/upgrade.mjs --project <legacy project id> (--persist-to DIR | --database D1 --bucket R2) once per workspace imported from legacy: it rewrites that workspace's legacy storage URLs to native URLs and applies the legacy widget translation where its settings are unchanged since import, under the workspace's import lease, printing counts only; a second run changes nothing.

pendingMigrations.buyerSteps: Back up D1 first; apply once after 321_legacy_import_files.sql, before serving the updated Worker. Additive only: creates the empty bs_retired table (value-free tombstones of team members erased from the installation: domain-separated SHA-256 digests of the roster address and the Business member id, with the invite number each had; never a name or address); no existing row changes and nothing is read, sent or queued. Without it, erasing a team member refuses with business_roster_missing_table:bs_retired. Nothing else to do: a team member erased by an earlier release leaves the Business roster at the Business's next signed revision.
